name: PT TBS Energi Utama Tbk

frontmatter.title: TBS Energi Utama — the disclosed waste-only accounts put the stock on HOLD
frontmatter.summary: The filed nine-month accounts disclose waste-only adjusted EBITDA of US$29.9m, which annualises to US$39.9m. The prior base used the waste-plus-EV US$42.0m share, double counting the US$1.6m EV earnings already in the Others book mark. Re-marked, waste equity is US$195.4m and the target Rp395, a 7.2% return; the Q3 run-rate is the tail case. Corrected: the mid-point, P/B and arithmetic slips. HOLD, target Rp395.
thesis: The base now uses the disclosed waste-only nine-month adjusted EBITDA of US$29.9m, annualised to US$39.9m, not the waste-plus-EV 71.0% share the prior draft capitalised [S27, F216, F221]. The US$1.6m EV residual is already inside the Others book mark, so capitalising it again in the waste multiple would count the same earnings twice (QC Q1). The Q3 waste-only quarter of US$6.3m annualises to US$25.2m and carries the bear weight, not the base [F222, F253].

The corrected SOTP is independent of the price: after the non-controlling interest, the US$10.6m closure provision and the 40.0% warranted discount, the marked parts are worth Rp361, against today's Rp368; the P/BV cross-check is Rp263. The blend gives a target of Rp395, a 7.2% return - HOLD [S0, F234].

Coal is marked at zero despite US$20.1m of nine-month coal EBITDA: the reserve is a short run-off, mine amortisation and sustaining capex absorb the cash, and the US$120.4m debt proxy costs more than the free cash flow [S25, F189].

Waste is the value, and the mark sits at the median of three independent anchors - the stock's own-history median, the Cora transaction [F240] and the live peer multiple - not a coal-era artefact. That mark gives US$195.4m of equity after the US$234.8m debt proxy, and the sensitivity band runs from Rp236 at the low end to Rp508 at the peer multiple [F116, F164, F204, F240].

The P/BV cross-check at Rp263 is the honest counterweight, and HPS is preference equity at SBTH: at an assumed high-single to low-double-digit coupon its annual claim is US$32.6m-US$49.0m, ranking ahead of the ordinary shares but adding no parent value on day one [S26].

blocks.text: **What changed and why.** This is a QC revision of the prior update. The company has since filed the nine-month consolidated accounts [S28], and the segment note makes the waste segment's own adjusted EBITDA directly observable: US$29.9m for the nine months [S27, F216]. The prior base capitalised the waste-plus-EV 71.0% share of the group figure - US$42.0m annualised - which included US$1.6m of electric-vehicle EBITDA already carried inside the Others book mark; that double count is removed (QC Q1) [F203, F221, F224]. Waste is now marked on the disclosed waste-only figure, US$39.9m annualised [F221]. The segment note shows waste revenue of US$157.3m on cost of revenue of US$136.3m - a 13.3% gross margin - and a segment operating loss of US$4.3m; above EBITDA sit a US$1.8m AEI goodwill impairment and US$1.7m of realised interest-rate-swap losses, and below EBITDA the finance-cost "others" line is US$15.4m against US$3.5m a year earlier [S28 p.96, p.141, p.149, Note 40]. The company's adjusted EBITDA already excludes the two above-EBITDA items, so they are not added back (QC Q2). The Q3 waste-only quarter of US$6.3m annualises to US$25.2m, not US$31.6m; it is the trough and the tail case [F222, F253, F145].

We therefore move TBS Energi Utama to **HOLD** with a twelve-month target of **Rp395**, a 7.2% return from the Rp368 price. The rating follows the corrected value, not a change of view on the transition: the base no longer annualises a single distorted quarter against a waste revenue line that rose 41.0% in the nine months [S27]. The SOTP at the 40.0% warranted discount is Rp361, the P/BV cross-check is Rp263, and the blend before the cost-of-equity roll-forward is Rp328. The operating distribution, weighted 25%/50%/25% across the Rp214 bear, the Rp394 base and the Rp608 bull, gives Rp403, also a HOLD [F157-F159].

The choice between the Q3 run-rate and the disclosed nine-month figure is shown, not hidden. On the Q3 waste-only quarter annualised (US$25.2m) the waste mark is US$37.1m and the target is Rp228, a SELL; on the disclosed nine-month figure the waste mark is US$195.4m and the target is Rp395, a HOLD [F86, F204, F245]. We use the disclosed nine-month actual because it is the segment's own reported figure; the Q3 number is a residual of two rounded percentage disclosures (US$6.3m) in a quarter that also carries the waste-entity refinancing [S27, S28, F222]. The midpoint arithmetic is also corrected: at the card midpoint the disclosed nine-month base gives Rp443, a BUY, while the Q3-trough midpoint - Rp249 after the closure provision - is a SELL at today's price [F205, F248].

The EV/EBITDA leg stays dropped. It was struck at DSSA's multiple - a konglo name whose listed premium the konglo card excludes from a parent's fundamental value - on group LTM EBITDA that includes the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero. The engine reads group EBITDA, and no waste-specific non-konglo comparator is registered, so the leg cannot be rebuilt premium-free on a segment-consistent base. The engine renormalises to 67% SOTP and 33% P/BV; the target is Rp395, a HOLD [S0, S11, S12, S25].

The breakeven marks are re-solved on the corrected base after the non-controlling interest: parity needs a post-NCI waste mark of US$170.1m, the HOLD floor US$135.1m and the SELL boundary US$82.5m. The US$10.6m nine-month reclamation and closure provision is now deducted at holdco, because coal is floored at zero and the liability would otherwise be omitted from every mark [S28 Note 26, F234]. The nine-month print supports the operating story - an 18.0% gross margin, adjusted EBITDA at 17.0% and operating cash flow of US$20.3m, with coal still contributing US$20.1m of EBITDA - and the waste re-mark is the correction the filed accounts support [S25, S28, F189].

The 40.0% discount is no longer justified by the old claim that the trailing P/B sits at its own mean. On 30 September parent equity the current trailing P/B is about 1.14x, well ABOVE the own-history mean (the 30 June book gives 1.01x), and the P/BV leg at Rp263 is -27.1% BELOW the SOTP, not above it as the prior draft said [S0, F235, F244, F250]. The top of the card's band is kept for the governance reasons below, not because the shares are optically cheap; the market-implied discount on the corrected NAV is about 38.8%, so the 40.0% base discount is slightly wider than what the price itself implies [F242]. The P/BV leg and the preference coupon are the counterweights, and the operating bear at Rp214 is the path to a SELL [S0, data/base_rates.yaml, F157].

TBS Energi Utama is an Indonesian energy group that began as a thermal-coal miner, listed in 2012 and renamed from Toba Bara Sejahtra in 2022 to mark a shift toward sustainable infrastructure. It reports in US dollars and runs five segments: coal mining, coal trading, waste management, a residual power book after the coal plants were sold, and an "others" line with palm oil, renewables and electric vehicles [S8, S9].

The mix has inverted. In the first half of 2026 waste produced 61.2% of revenue and 91.8% of adjusted EBITDA; by the nine months waste and electric vehicles together were 66.0% of revenue and 71.0% of adjusted EBITDA, and waste alone earned US$157.3m of revenue at a 13.3% gross margin [S12, S25]. Coal is smaller but not negligible in the P&L: mining revenue US$61.8m, gross profit US$21.6m and EBITDA US$20.1m, while trading is down to US$19.5m with a small EBITDA loss [S25]. Waste carries most of the acquired goodwill because it was built by acquisition [S12].

The waste platform, under SBTH Asia Holdings, operates three brands: Cora Environment, a Singapore municipal and commercial collector formerly Sembcorp Environment, with an energy-from-waste plant of about 360,000 tonnes a year; Asia Medical Enviro Services, with about 45.0% of the Singapore medical-waste market; and Arah Environmental in Indonesian medical, industrial and household waste across 15.0 provinces [S9, S10]. Together they collected 755,990 tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, and the economics rest on collection density, permitted facilities and long municipal contracts [S25, S22, S10]. The 2 November update attributes 743,600 tonnes of that total to Cora and reports more than 30m beverage containers processed under Singapore's Beverage Container Return Scheme - density and permit evidence rather than a new revenue line [S27]. The tonnage disclosures do not fully reconcile - the first-half presentation gives a larger six-month figure [S15], the nine-month release 755,990 tonnes [S22] and the 2 November article attributes 743,600 tonnes of the nine-month total to Cora alone [S27] - so they are scale evidence, not a modelled volume series; the implied negative Q3 collection is a source inconsistency, not an input (QC note on facts).

Coal is smaller than the balance sheet suggests: about 7,087 hectares across three East Kalimantan mines run through ABN, IM and TMU, with reserves of about 14 Mt against planned production of 3-4 Mt a year [S9]. In the first half the mines produced 0.8 Mt and sold 0.6 Mt at an average price of US$55.2/ton against a FOB cash cost of US$38.2/ton and a stripping ratio of 3.2x [S12].

The other legs are real but sub-scale: a 6 MW mini-hydro plant, a 46 MWp floating-solar project that was 65.0 complete at the half-year, 13,883 Electrum electric two-wheelers and a 2,185 hectare plantation [S12, S9]. Highland holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0% through a Singapore trust, leaving a 31.7% residual; the controlling block sets strategy and how much cash reaches the parent [S9].

TBS straddles two industries with little in common. Thermal coal is a mature, price-taking export business; waste management is a recurring, contract-based service with local density advantages; waste is now the dominant earnings driver even though coal still supplies much of the collateral [S9, S12].

The coal arm is cyclical and small. TBS's realised price of US$55.2/ton sits below the headline HBA and ICI benchmarks because its grades are lower and its mix includes trading volumes, and the FOB cash cost of US$38.2/ton leaves a thin margin; the segment ran an operating loss in the first half [S12, S11]. With about 14.0 Mt of reserves against planned production of 3-4 Mt a year, the coal arm should be valued as a declining cash harvest, not on a stable multiple [S9].

Coal regulation matters three ways: the progressive royalty sets a floor under unit costs, the domestic market obligation requires a share of output at capped prices, and environmental licensing governs expansion and closure. Policy is pushing Indonesia away from coal generation while still relying on it for baseload, a long noisy transition rather than a clean exit [S9].

Waste is the opposite: a recurring service with high local density economics, long municipal contracts and permitted facilities hard to replicate. Singapore's collection is split into geographic sectors, Cora holds two, and its energy-from-waste plant turns non-recyclable waste into industrial steam; AMES's compliance moat gives it about 45.0% of the medical-waste market, while Arah serves a fragmenting Indonesian market [S10, S12, S9]. Competition is local and consolidating, with permits, density and disposal capacity as barriers rather than capital alone; the risk is that the acquisition-led roll-up pays rising multiples faster than it earns synergies, which is where the HPS capital will go [S10, S15]. Renewables are contracted but small, and the EV business lacks a proven durable margin [S12, S9].

External influences are macro and regulatory: dollar reporting, Singapore-dollar waste revenue and rupiah debt mean USD/SGD, USD/IDR and Indonesian rates all matter. The look-through factors - coal, Indonesian rates, Singapore waste demand, USD/SGD and domestic EV and plantation demand - are recorded for sizing [S9, S10, S12].

Revenue fell from US$635.8m in FY2022 to US$365.9m in FY2025 as coal normalised and power moved toward divestment, and gross profit fell faster, from US$136.0m to US$29.7m [S0, S8]. FY2025 also carries a divestment loss of about US$96.9m and a net loss of US$161.9m [S17, S8].

The first half of 2026 shows the post-divestment business: revenue US$173.0m, gross profit more than doubled to US$28.2m, adjusted EBITDA US$25.7m and operating cash flow positive at US$14.6m [S12, S11]. The company's nine-month release extends it: revenue US$257.3m, gross profit US$45.2m at 18.0%, adjusted EBITDA up 39.0% to US$44.4m at a 17.0% margin, the parent loss narrowing 72.0% to US$35.4m, operating cash flow US$20.3m and cash US$89.6m [S25]. It is still an EBITDA improvement, not an earnings improvement: D&A, the Cora acquisition and the refinancing one-off exceed operating profit [S25]. On the engine definition used throughout, model EBITDA is EBIT plus D&A; FY2025A model EBITDA of US$43.2m compares with the company's US$47.2m adjusted figure, the difference being the adjustments the company adds back (QC note on the EBITDA definition) [S8, S17]. Equity was US$172.0m against US$751.7m of assets and US$579.6m of liabilities at 30 September 2026; gross debt is not disclosed in the release, and the last balance-sheet figure is US$399.3m at 30 June [S20, S25, S11].

The 2 November article fills the segment gap in that release: waste adjusted EBITDA was US$29.9m on US$157.3m of revenue, a 19.0% margin, which reconciles to the 71.0% waste-plus-EV share of the US$44.4m group figure and leaves US$1.6m for electric vehicles [S27, F181, F141]. Against the disclosed US$111.9m of prior-year waste revenue the growth is the stated 41.0% [S27]. The segment margin exceeds the 13.3% waste gross margin because the segment's depreciation and amortisation sit in cost of revenue; it is an EBITDA margin, not a cash margin [S25, S27].

Waste produced US$155.4m of FY2025 revenue and most of the first half, while coal mining and trading contributed about a third at a low margin [S3, S12]. We set FY2026E growth at -6.6% - the nine months of US$257.3m plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate gives US$341.6m - then 6.0% and 5.0% as waste annualises; no large acquisition is assumed [S25, S12, S26].

We anchor FY2026E gross margin at the exact nine-month 17.6% and operating expenses at the first-half run-rate of 17.9% of revenue, because the data pack's SG&A is too low (FY2025 selling and G&A about US$72.0m, first half US$33.2m) [S8, S12, S25]. The blended margin is mix, not waste economics: waste earns 13.3% while coal mining's gross profit is US$21.6m on US$61.8m of revenue [S25]. The group is EBITDA-positive but EBIT-negative at the run-rate, the arithmetic of a capital-intensive transition. FY2026E carries a one-off refinancing charge, and the filed nine-month accounts now size most of it: the finance-cost "others" line is US$15.4m against US$3.5m a year earlier, a step of US$11.9m that is the visible refinancing cost at the waste entities [S28 Note 40, F232, F251, F252]. We keep the explicit range around that step rather than a figure sized solely to reconcile the parent loss of US$35.4m, because the cash/non-cash split is still not disclosed [S25]. The charge is inside forecast net debt as a cash cost; if it proves non-cash or is amortised, net debt is lower and the SOTP is unaffected because the marks do not use the forecast loss.

The data pack's D&A was the G&A charge only. The audited notes show fixed-asset depreciation US$22.2m, mine-property amortisation US$31.3m, right-of-use depreciation US$11.8m and intangibles US$8.8m, a full charge of US$74.1m [S8]. The nine-month release does not print a single D&A line, but the filed nine-month income statement does: revenue US$257.3m, gross profit US$45.2m, selling and G&A at the filed nine-month ratio and a small operating loss. Adjusted EBITDA of US$44.4m is EBIT plus D&A plus the above-EBITDA one-offs, so nine-month D&A is 16.0% of revenue [S28 p.8, S25]. The forecast uses that filed ratio, with SG&A at the same filed rate, not the first-half inference the prior draft carried and not the FY2025 charge that includes divested-PLTU depreciation [S8, S12, S25].

FY2025 operating cash flow was US$5.2m with capex of US$47.1m; the first half improved to US$14.6m against fixed-asset capex of US$10.2m, and nine-month operating cash flow was US$20.3m [S8, S11, S25]. The release does not split nine-month capex, so we keep capex at 10.0% of revenue falling to 8.0% and net borrowing of US$15.0m and US$10.0m [S13, S25]. Net debt was US$307.3m at FY2025 and about 5.4x adjusted EBITDA at the half; cash rose to US$89.6m at 30 September but gross debt is undisclosed, and the refinancing extends maturity, not leverage [S8, S12, S13, S25]. On the disclosed cash and the rise in total liabilities, the 30 September net debt proxy is US$313.8m, essentially flat in dollars; because equity fell, leverage is higher. The valuation section shows a symmetric debt-proxy sensitivity, and the SOTP marks use the 30 June proxies until a gross-debt figure is disclosed [F208].

Cash conversion deteriorated: operating cash flow over restated EBITDA was 1.41 in FY2024, 0.12 in FY2025 and 0.46 in the first nine months, and the negative accruals ratio is mechanical from the non-cash divestment loss [S8, S24]. Goodwill is US$85.5m, about half of parent equity, and the price is 2.06 times tangible book [S11]. The former Highland receivable of US$37.7m was assigned to CDG Trading at 6.8% and sits in US$43.2m of third-party receivables with CDG's ownership undisclosed; we classify it optics-class and apply the half-haircut (Rp263), showing the full write-off (Rp224) against reported book (Rp302); the same half-haircut now sits in the SOTP "others" mark, so the two legs are consistent [S8, S11].

The holdco card calls for a sum of the parts with honest marks, less holdco net debt, less a discount treated as the base rate, not the opportunity; TBS fits it better than a consolidated multiple, which would price the mix and the leverage together [S0].

Cost of equity builds from a risk-free rate of 4.9%, an equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country premium of 2.5%, and a beta of 0.9 levered to 2.3, giving a cost of equity of 20.3% and a WACC of 10.4% [S0].

Each part is an equity value: coal after its own debt proxy, waste on an EV/EBITDA multiple after its debt proxy, trading and power at book, and others at book less the same half-haircut the P/BV leg carries [S11, S12]. The deductions are the non-controlling interest of US$21.8m, against an ABN claim of US$29.1m, and the US$10.6m nine-month mine reclamation and closure provision [S11 p.137, S28 Note 26]. The provision is a consolidated obligation of the run-off coal segment; because coal is floored at zero, deducting it at holdco is the only place it can enter, and it is not inside the coal debt proxy, which is built from segment finance costs [F234]. The full net NCI figure is conservative because coal is marked at zero [S11 p.137]. The US$307.1m book elimination is the consolidation wedge, not third-party debt, and deducting it again was the prior FATAL [S11 p.150].

Coal is zero despite US$20.1m of nine-month coal EBITDA. The rebuilt run-off uses the actual segment volume, price and cash cost: the 14 Mt reserve at the current sales run-rate gives a life of about nine years, while the 3-4 Mt/yr plan gives a shorter four-year life. On the observed volume the free cash flow after sustaining capex and cash tax is a few million dollars a year, and the US$120.4m debt proxy costs more than that, so the equity floors at zero [F207]. Without the debt proxy the same DCF is positive, but the proxy would then have to be deducted at holdco, leaving the SOTP unchanged; the plan-volume upper bound is about the same size as the proxy. The red team is right that the proxy is an allocation, not a secured claim; it is still the only honest way to allocate the group's US$399.3m debt across the parts [S25, S9, S11, F85, F207].

Waste now uses the disclosed waste-only nine-month figure, not the waste-plus-EV share and not the Q3 trough. The nine-month LK shows the segment earned US$157.3m of revenue at a 13.3% gross margin and lost US$4.3m at the operating line, with a US$1.8m AEI goodwill impairment and US$1.7m of realised interest-rate-swap losses above EBITDA and a US$15.4m finance-cost "others" line below it [S28 p.96, p.141, p.149]. The company's adjusted EBITDA definition already excludes those above-EBITDA items, so adding them back would double count (QC Q2). The directly disclosed waste-only adjusted EBITDA is US$29.9m for the nine months, which annualises to US$39.9m [S27, F216, F221]. The waste-plus-EV 71.0% share annualises to US$42.0m, higher by the US$1.6m EV residual; because that residual is already inside the Others book mark, capitalising it in the waste multiple would count the same earnings twice (QC Q1). The quarterly path is the first half US$23.6m and the third quarter US$6.3m; the Q3 quarter annualises to US$25.2m, which is the trough and the bear [F222, F241, F253]. At the own-history median multiple the disclosed base gives a US$195.4m equity mark after the US$234.8m debt proxy; the Q3 annualisation gives US$37.1m and the target Rp228 [F86, F204, F245]. The multiple is the median of the own-history median, the 8.86x Cora transaction and the live peer median from the 4 November 2026 datapack, not a coal-era artefact [S0, S8 p.84, F236-F240]. At the Cora transaction equity value the target is Rp264, below the base, which is why the base does not assume HPS is deployed at once [S8, F165]. No premium-free listed waste comparator is registered; the full sensitivity band is shown below.

The debt proxies are 30 June figures. At 30 September the release gives cash of US$89.6m and a higher liability total but no gross debt; the net debt proxy is US$313.8m, close to the 30 June level, so dollar leverage is flat while equity is lower [S20, F208]. A symmetric move of five per cent in the waste and coal debt proxies takes the target to Rp382 on the high-side and Rp407 on the low-side, i.e. a HOLD and an ADD respectively, so the rating does not depend on the proxy rounding; the base keeps the 30 June proxies because no newer gross-debt figure is disclosed [F214, F215].

The card also requires holdco opex capitalised at about ten times. We have tested it and do not deduct it again. The Q2 segment note reconciles the consolidated selling and G&A charge of US$33.2m to the five segments with no unallocated corporate column, and the waste mark is struck on adjusted EBITDA after segment G&A while the coal run-off uses segment costs after selling and G&A [S11 p.145, S12]. Capitalising the same group cost a second time would double count it. The residual is the "others" book mark, which is carried at net assets less the receivable haircut; if some corporate cost is embedded there it is not separately capitalised, and that is a disclosed limitation rather than a hidden deduction.

The "others" mark now carries the same half-haircut as the P/BV leg: book net assets of US$94.3m less liabilities of US$50.7m less the half of the US$43.2m related-party receivable, giving a materially lower book mark than the full net-asset figure. The full write-off is a downside case at about Rp224 on the P/BV leg and a lower SOTP; the receivable is an optics-class flag, not a manipulation-class one, so a half-haircut is the base [S8, F89, F167].

The SOTP is translated at the data pack's spot USD/IDR of Rp18,140/USD, not the reviewed macro deck's FY2027E rate of Rp18,350/USD. The marks are dated at 30 June and 30 September, the target is a twelve-month value, and using a forward rate would require re-stating the rupiah debt service on the same basis; the rate difference moves the target by only a few rupiah a share, so spot is the consistent basis and the choice is not rating-moving [S0]. The model reads no deck driver: the coal benchmark, Indonesian rates and USD/SGD waste revenue are recorded as look-through exposures, not forecast drivers, because the SOTP marks are dated holdings values rather than a consolidated multiple. The thermal-coal NEUTRAL overlay is consistent with a zero coal mark - we are not forecasting a coal-price collapse, we find no equity value after the debt proxy, the closure provision and the short reserve life [S0, S12, S25].

The blend is 67% SOTP and 33% P/BV. P/BV at the 0.83 peer median gives Rp263, -27.1% below the SOTP; the gap is book quality - already net of the half-haircut (US$145.6m against reported US$167.2m), with US$85.5m of goodwill and the divestment loss [S0, S8, S11]. The median is the trailing P/B of the eleven registered CONGLOMERATES packs at their 30 June 2026 balance sheets and current datapack prices, and the same figure holds on the eleven-name set and on the ADRO/DSSA/IMJS subset; it is not the forward FY2026E multiple the published comps table prints for TOBA itself, and the red team's higher figure is that forward-book variant, worth only a few rupiah a share [S0]. The P/BV leg is struck on 30 June parent equity after the half-haircut; moving it to 30 September parent equity would take it about Rp34 lower, and the base stays on the reported, audited book because it is the cleaner cross-check [F176, F244]. The EV/EBITDA leg is removed; P/E is unavailable on negative trailing earnings and no dividend is forecast, so the honest set is the primary plus one cross-check [S0].

The P/BV leg is also stressed on the forecast book, because the model is EBIT-negative at the current margin structure and the book erodes. On FY2027E book the leg is Rp225 and on FY2028E book lower again; a full impairment of the US$85.5m goodwill takes it to Rp108 [F209, F210]. The operating-leverage path is real - the non-cash coal mine amortisation and the coal segment's G&A roll off as the reserves deplete - but the model holds the ratios flat, so the forecast understates that improvement. We treat the forecast-book stress as a downside cross-check and keep the base leg on current reported book; the primary SOTP does not depend on the P/BV leg [S8, S11, F13, F209, F210].

The base discount is 40.0%, the top of the card's band, not the price's own implied discount. The old figure was reverse-solved from the 30 October price, so the SOTP leg equalled the price by construction and carried no independent information [S0, S25]. The company does not publish a historical SOTP and the data pack has no NAV series, so the five-year discount-to-NAV range the card asks for cannot be sourced; the closest own-history series is P/BV, whose mean and median the model tracks across the FY2022 to FY2025 observations [S0]. The current trailing P/B is 1.14x on 30 September parent equity - well ABOVE that mean, not at it; on 30 June book it is 1.01x - so the prior "at the mean" claim is corrected and the top of the band is not defended as an optical discount [S0, F235, F244, F250]. It is warranted by governance and upstream coverage: the controlling trust, the undisclosed related-party receivable, the HPS preference ranking ahead of the ordinary and the thin dividend-upstream coverage proxy [S9, S8, S26, F163]. The market-implied discount on the corrected NAV is about 38.8%, just inside the 40.0% top of the card band, so the base discount is slightly wider than the market's own level rather than outside it [F242]. At the band midpoint the target is Rp443, a BUY; the base is Rp395 [data/base_rates.yaml].

Holding coal at zero and the discount fixed, price parity needs a post-NCI waste mark of US$170.1m; the HOLD floor is US$135.1m and the SELL boundary US$82.5m [F113, F119, F120]. At the low end of the waste band the target is Rp236, a SELL; at the twelve-turn level Rp445, at the live peer multiple Rp508 and at the Cora anchor Rp264 [F116, F117, F164, F165]. At the true Q3 trough (US$25.2m annualised) and the low-end multiple, waste equity floors at zero and the target is Rp175 at the wider discount - the tail case, disclosed rather than used as the central bear (QC Q3) [F253, F254].

The discount-only bear is Rp346 and the bull Rp443 [S12, S15]. The driver corners are wider - Rp214 for a SELL when waste is at the low end, coal zero and the discount widens, and Rp608 for a BUY at the peer multiple with coal at its plan upper bound - and the probability-weighted driver target, on the same scenario weights, is Rp403 [F157-F159]. Unlike the old distribution, the weighted figure is now a HOLD: the disclosed nine-month base carries the centre of the probability mass, and the coal-zero floor limits how far the bear corner can fall, but the bull corner is not wide enough to lift the weighted target into ADD territory.

HPS commits up to S$555m to SBTH in multiple tranches through newly issued preference shares and other instruments, subject to EGMS approval, with TBS retaining control [S26]. It is equity, not debt: it does not enter holdco net debt and there is no bridge line, because a fair-value preference subscription adds cash and an equal prior claim. It sits inside SBTH, below the waste equity mark, which is the ordinary/common equity after that claim; it creates parent value only through what the cash earns [S26, S10]. The coupon is undisclosed; at an assumed high-single to low-double-digit rate the annual claim is US$32.6m-US$49.0m against US$44.4m of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, so it is mezzanine-like in ranking while still preferred equity [S26, F101, F102]. The conversion sensitivity is explicit: a range of common-equivalent stakes would take the target to Rp374, Rp354 and Rp333 - a HOLD in each case, not the REDUCE the prior draft claimed - so a conversion of a third of the waste equity removes any remaining upside but does not on its own break the ordinary shares [F211-F213]. That is why the bear case treats the ordinary equity as worth little until the coupon is covered, while the base adds no headline value at inception.

**Regulatory risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: the royalty schedule, domestic market obligation and environmental licensing can change the coal arm's unit economics, and the waste franchise depends on municipal contracts and permits in two jurisdictions [S9, S10]. **Commodity risk** is high-likelihood and medium-impact: TBS is a price-taker, so a weaker ICI complex would compress the coal cash harvest before waste offsets it [S12, S9]. **Execution risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: the waste platform is acquisition-led, the HPS money is staged, and the solar project must reach commercial operation on schedule [S12, S10].

**Governance risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: Highland holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0% through a Singapore trust, and a preference claim ranks ahead of the ordinary at the waste subsidiary; the inbreng was completed without a fairness opinion because the entities are almost wholly owned [S9, S10, S16]. **Liquidity risk** is medium-likelihood and medium-impact: the residual outside the controlling holders is 31.7%, and the average daily traded value of IDR13.9bn is thin against a market capitalisation of IDR3,057.9bn [S0]. **Currency and rate risk** is medium-likelihood and medium-impact: dollar reporting, Singapore-dollar waste revenue and rupiah debt mean a stronger dollar or higher Indonesian rates compress translated value [S8, S13]. **Coal reserve risk** is the quiet one: a short reserve life turns the cash harvest into a run-off if reserves are not replaced [S9].

The bear case is now an operating bear, not only a discount shock. It assumes the market pays the low-end multiple on the disclosed nine-month waste base with a ten-point wider holdco discount, giving Rp214, a SELL [F157]. If the Q3 waste-only run-rate persists rather than reverting - the US$6.3m quarter annualised to US$25.2m - waste equity floors at zero at that multiple and the tail case is Rp175, shown in section four rather than carried as the central bear [F222, F253, F254]. In that world the ordinary equity earns nothing until waste EBITDA covers the preference coupon and segment interest, and the "others" book mark carries the related-party receivable at half value with the US$85.5m goodwill unimpaired. Leverage is 5.4x net loans to adjusted EBITDA at the half, cash conversion is 0.46 operating cash flow to EBITDA at the nine months, and a coupon at the low end of the assumed range would absorb more than half of the nine-month annualised adjusted EBITDA [S12, S25, F101, F102, F156]. A common-equivalent HPS conversion of a third of the waste equity takes the target to Rp333, a HOLD [F213]. On a full goodwill impairment the P/BV leg is Rp108 [F210]. None of these is the base, but together they are the path to the SELL corner at Rp214 [F157].

The dated bull case the red team asked for is HPS deployed at the Cora-like multiple, the solar project reaching commercial operation on its stated schedule and waste revenue compounding. The HPS commitment is a dated EGMS event and the funds are earmarked for Asian waste expansion; the floating-solar project was 65.0 complete with commercial operation targeted for the fourth quarter [S26, S12]. If the HPS capital is deployed at the peer multiple and waste revenue grows at its nine-month rate, the waste mark moves toward the Rp508 target at the warranted discount and the Rp608 corner with the discount at the card midpoint [F164, F158]. The engine's discount-only bull of Rp443 does not include the deployment, which is why the operating bull carries its own weight. We do not treat the EGMS itself as a discount-narrowing catalyst: it authorises a preference issuance that ranks ahead of the ordinary, so it changes the capital structure before it changes the discount [S26, F195]. We value the HPS money at zero at inception in the base, which the red team accepted as an alternative only if justified - it is the ordinary/common equity after the preference claim, and the terms are undisclosed, so paying for the cash before it is invested and before the coupon is known would double-count the deployment upside [S26, S10].

The engine table mirrors the same driver, the holdco discount, at probabilities of 25.0%, 50.0% and 25.0%, giving Rp346, Rp395 and Rp443 [S12, S15]. That table shocks only the discount; the engine cannot re-price dated holdings from a model input, so the operating distribution is carried as computed facts on the same weights: the disclosed nine-month base at the low-end multiple and a ten-point wider discount gives Rp214, weighted 25%; the nine-month base at the own-history median multiple and the warranted discount gives Rp394, weighted 50%; and HPS deployed at the peer multiple with coal at its plan upper bound and the discount at the card midpoint gives Rp608, weighted 25% - a weighted Rp403 [F157-F159]. The base target the engine reports is Rp395; the operating re-weight is slightly higher because the bull corner is wider than the discount-only bull, and both are HOLD. A SELL requires the waste multiple to compress to the low end while the discount widens, the mirrored operating downside, not the central path [S12, S0].

The signposts that would change our view are specific: a segment disclosure letting us mark waste on its own cash flows; a completed, priced acquisition showing the HPS money deployed accretively; a reserve upgrade or long-term offtake extending mine life; and a dated discount-narrowing event such as a buyback, tender or structural dividend increase from the waste subsidiary [S10, S15]. On the other side, a preference term sheet giving HPS conversion or upside participation at the expense of the ordinary would widen the discount, not narrow it [S10, S15].

Control is concentrated and the structure opaque at the top. Highland Strategic Holdings holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0%; Highland is owned by GLAS Trust, a Singapore trust acting for a passive private investment trust, and no single individual holds more than half [S9]. The annual report leaves 31.7% outside those holders; the data pack's free-float and insider fields overlap and sum above one hundred per cent, so we use the filing composition [S9]. Minorities have little influence over strategy, related-party terms or the pace of the transition [S9].

The auditor is KAP Purwantono, Sungkoro & Surja, an EY member, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements signed by the board on 9 March 2026 [S9]. Related-party dealings are small in the reported numbers but structurally important. At FY2024 the group carried a non-current receivable from Highland of US$37.7m under an acknowledgement extended to eighteen years and then assigned on 30 June 2025 to CDG Trading at 6.8%; the balance now sits in US$43.2m of non-current third-party receivables, and CDG's ownership and relationship to the controller are not disclosed [S8]. Interest income from Highland was US$0.7m in FY2025, so the receivable is not dead, but the assignment to an undisclosed third party is exactly the channel through which value can move between affiliates; we classify it optics-class and apply the haircut in the P/BV leg [S8].

On 16 October 2026 the group moved its SBT shares through SBTI, SBTH and SBTG at a stated S$138.2m with no fairness opinion because the entities are almost wholly owned [S16]. It is an intra-group subscription price, not an appraisal, so we treat it as a weak marker; the sequencing matters because the waste opco sits under SBTH immediately before HPS takes preference shares there, directing the claim at the whole platform [S10, S16].

On exchange status, the shares were suspended for one trading day on 18 June 2025 after a significant cumulative price rise, and the suspension on the Regular and Cash Markets was lifted from Session I on 19 June 2025; the annual report discloses no other suspension or delisting proceeding, so there is no current special notation to adjust the valuation for [S9 p.12].

On pledges, the company's shares in operating subsidiaries and its accounts, receivables and inventories are collateral for the ADB, TLB and SEF facilities, while the controlling shareholder's TOBA shares are not disclosed as pledged; a subsidiary pledge is normal project finance, a controlling-block pledge would be a margin-call supply risk [S9]. The group paid US$17.5m of dividends in FY2025 including minorities despite a net loss, and the trailing DPS is Rp18.6; we assume the dividend is suspended on our negative near-term earnings [S8, S0]. ESG is central rather than incidental: the strategy is a decarbonisation transition, the PLTU divestments cut emissions by about 80.0%, and the waste platform is the environmental-services asset, while governance is the weak link that has to earn its discount rather than assume it away [S9, S10, S16].

Indonesian holding companies owned through family or trust structures have long traded at persistent discounts to the value of the assets they control, because minorities depend on cash actually upstreamed and control rarely changes hands. A transition story can narrow the discount for a while, but the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity.

The nearest dated catalysts are the shareholder meeting to approve the HPS preference investment and the floating-solar commercial operation date [S15, S12]. The HPS transaction is the more important: the preference terms, the staging schedule and the first acquisition will tell us whether the waste platform's capital is raised on terms that leave value for the ordinary shareholder [S10, S15]. The capital remains pending - management says the impact depends on fund realisation and expansion effectiveness - so the first drawdown and first acquisition, not the announcement, are the events that would move the waste mark [S27, F223]. The KPIs we monitor are waste revenue and adjusted EBITDA share, Cora's collected tonnage and plant availability, coal cash cost and stripping ratio, the reserve statement, net debt to adjusted EBITDA, the holdco discount to our SOTP, and the HPS deployment schedule [S12, S9, S10]. We also watch related-party disclosures and any change in the preference terms, the channels through which waste value reaches the parent's ordinary shareholders [S8, S16]. Until a dated event or a waste re-rate changes the arithmetic, the balance of evidence supports **HOLD** at the current price [S10, S15].

bear.narrative: The holdco discount widens ten points to 50%, above the card's band: the Q3 waste margin persists rather than reverting, the HPS money is deployed slowly and the preference coupon absorbs waste cash, so the market pays less for the parts. This table shocks the discount only - the SOTP marks are dated holdings values and the consolidated forecast does not re-price them - and the report states that limitation plainly; the operating downside is shown separately as a driver-based corner (waste 7x, coal zero, 50% discount), which is the SELL path and carries a weight in the re-weighted operating distribution in section 5.

bull.narrative: The holdco discount narrows ten points to 30%, the middle of the card's band, as the HPS preference is approved and drawn, the money is deployed at a Cora-like waste multiple, coal cash cost stays low and the floating solar reaches COD on time. This table shocks the discount only, as the report states; the driver-based bull corner (waste 13.51x, coal +US$26m, 30% discount) is shown separately in section 4 and carries the 25% bull weight in the re-weighted operating distribution in section 5.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 consolidated revenue was US$257.3m, 11% below the prior-year period, because the legacy coal business shrank faster than waste grew; the company's own release confirms this [S25, F179]. The nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the 2026 third-quarter run-rate of US$84.3m gives FY2026E of about US$341.6m, which is -6.6% against the FY2025 continuing-operations base of US$365.9m, not the -12% used before: the old figure implied a fourth quarter of US$64.7m, below every quarter of 2026 [S25, F1, F179]. We then return to 6%/5%/4%/3% as the HPS-funded waste build annualises and the 46 MWp floating solar starts producing [S25, S26, S12].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the latest actual: the company's 9M2026 release shows gross profit of US$45.2m on US$257.3m of revenue, which is 17.6% (the company rounds it to 18%), more than double the prior-year period's 8%, with waste plus electric vehicles at 66% of revenue [S25, F179, F180]. The waste segment's own gross margin is 13.3% while coal mining earned 35%; the blended ratio is therefore a mix outcome, not a waste margin [S25, F186, F188]. We anchor FY2026E at the exact 17.6% and hold it — there is no sourced reason for a margin fade, and a further uplift from waste mix is left to the bull case [S25].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's 11.4% is wrong: the LK shows selling and G&A expenses of US$71.95m against US$380.2m of segment revenue in FY2025 (18.9% of the reported US$365.9m consolidated revenue) [S17, F96]. The filed 9M2026 income statement is the later actual and is lower: selling US$0.283m plus G&A US$45.910m = US$46.193m on US$257.345m of revenue, 17.95% [S28 p.8]. We use the 9M actual of 17.95% for all forecast years rather than the 1H rate of 19.2% that the prior base held, because the later filed statement supersedes the half-year inference (QC Q5/Q10).

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The filed 9M2026 income statement fixes the charge directly: revenue US$257.345m, gross profit US$45.198m, selling and G&A US$46.193m (17.95%) and an operating loss of US$0.431m. Adjusted EBITDA of US$44.4m is EBIT plus D&A plus US$3.536m of above-EBITDA one-offs, so 9M D&A is about US$41.3m, 16.0% of revenue [S28 p.8, S25, F162]. The two above-EBITDA items (AEI goodwill impairment US$1.789m and the realised swap loss US$1.747m) are already excluded from the company's adjusted EBITDA, so the 16.0% is derived from the actual SG&A and D&A, not by holding SG&A at the 1H rate (QC Q5). The 1H 2026 ratio was 17.6% and the full FY2025 charge of US$74.121m (20.3%, F81) included divested-PLTU depreciation; neither is the forward run-rate [S8, S12]. We use 16.0% for all forecast years: D&A is a fixed accounting ratio here, not a growth driver.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was US$47.1m (12.9% of revenue), including mine-property additions of US$37.2m and fixed assets of US$9.8m [S8]. The 46 MWp floating-solar project is 65% complete with COD targeted for Q4 2026, so capex stays elevated: 10% in FY2026E, 9% in FY2027E and 8% long run [S12].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was US$9.1m on US$365.9m of revenue (2.5%), and the group describes disciplined working-capital management [S8, S3]. We hold 3.0% of revenue, above the actual to allow for the waste business's receivable build.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025's effective rate is meaningless on a loss; FY2024 paid US$14.1m on US$36.9m of pre-tax profit (38.2%), above the 22% statutory rate because of non-deductible items [S8]. We use the 22% statutory rate on positive pre-tax profit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs were US$26.0m on opening debt of US$341.9m (7.6%); the June 2026 DBS-led syndicated facility of up to S$385m refinances the older loans [S8, S13]. We use 7.5% on opening debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income was US$3.9m on opening cash of US$67.8m (5.8%); 1H 2026 interest income was US$2.8m [S8, S12]. We use 5.5% on opening cash.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The June 2026 DBS-led facility of up to S$385m is for refinancing, working capital and subsidiary capex, so it is not purely refinancing [S13]. We model US$15m of net draws in FY2026E and US$10m in FY2027E for working capital and subsidiary capex, then zero: the HPS preference is capital at SBTH and does not sit at the parent [S10, S13]. The quarter-end debt line was flat ($392.9m at FY2025 vs $393.0m at 1H 2026), which caps the near-term draw [S8, S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the refinancing one-off at the waste entities. The 9M2026 LK now sizes most of it: the finance-cost "other" line is US$15.425m against US$3.525m in the prior-year period, a US$11.900m step after the SBT Invest/Taonga facility was refinanced on 3 July 2026 [S28 Note 40, S28 Note 35]. We carry US$11.9m as a non-operating charge, below the old US$18m plug; the exact cash/non-cash split is still not disclosed, and if part is amortised the forecast net debt is lower by that amount, with no effect on the SOTP because the marks do not use the forecast loss. The LK also shows US$1.789m of AEI goodwill impairment and US$1.747m of realised interest-rate-swap losses in other operating expenses, above EBIT; those are excluded from the recurring forecast and added back in the waste-mark discussion [S28 Notes 18, 39, 41]. Zero thereafter: the FY2025 PLTU divestment loss (US$96.9m) and the FX loss are non-recurring and excluded [S8, S17].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities were 40.7% of FY2024 net profit and the minority balance sheet interest is US$21.8m (about 11% of equity) at 1H 2026 [S8, S11]. At 9M2026 the total loss of US$40.05m against the US$35.4m parent loss implies the minorities absorbed about US$4.65m, 11.6% [S25, F126, F182]. We use 12%, anchored on that last actual rather than the old 25%. The HPS preference is preferred equity inside SBTH, not a non-controlling interest in the consolidated P&L, so it does not justify a higher minority percentage; its drag is carried in the SOTP mark and the conversion sensitivity instead [S26, S28].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash dividends were US$17.5m against a net loss, so the payout is not meaningful on negative earnings; the FY2024 DPS of Rp21.98 was paid out of a US$28.5m parent profit [S8, S0]. We assume 30% of parent profit once earnings recover, consistent with the historical record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares rose from 8,249.4m at FY2025 to 8,309.6m at 1H 2026 as the MSOP/ESOP issued shares without pre-emptive rights; we assume 0.5% a year [S8, S11, S9].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zeroed per QC round-2 Q2. The holdco_sotp target is SOTP plus a P/BV cross-check; no DCF method runs, so terminal growth drives nothing and the old 2.0% was an unconnected input. The field stays at zero so the engine's input contract is met without implying a growth assumption the valuation does not use [S0].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: The base is the top of the card's 20-40% band, not the 45% the price happened to imply. The prior 45% was reverse-solved from the 30 October price, so the SOTP leg equalled the price by construction and carried no independent information [S0, S25]. The company does not publish a historical SOTP and the data pack has no NAV series, so a true five-year discount-to-NAV range cannot be sourced; the closest own-history series is P/BV (FY2022 0.929x, FY2023 0.489x, FY2024 0.566x, FY2025A 1.882x, mean 0.966x, median 0.748x [S0]). On 30 September 2026 parent equity the current trailing P/B is about 1.14x (F235), about 17% ABOVE that own mean, not at it; the earlier "0.93x, at the mean" sentence was wrong and is corrected. The stock is also above the 0.83x trailing peer median on book [S0], so a narrow discount is not what the market is paying. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §2 sets 20-40% as the persistent base rate; 40% is the warranted top because the governance discount has not been earned away: Highland Strategic Holdings holds 60.356% through a Singapore trust and PT Toba Sejahtra another 7.975% [S9], the US$43.2m receivable sits with an undisclosed related party [S8], and the HPS preference ranks ahead of the ordinary at the waste subsidiary [S26, F195]. The dividend-upstream coverage proxy is only 1.22x nine-month operating cash flow against the annualised rule-of-thumb distribution, so the parent depends on subsidiary cash it does not control directly [F163]. There is no dated, completed narrowing catalyst: HPS is newly issued preference equity at SBTH, a financing rather than a cash distribution, and still needs EGMS approval [S26, F195, F197]. The market-implied discount on the corrected SOTP is about 38.8% (F242), just inside the 40% card top: the base is the warranted top and is close to, not wide of, the market's own level. Section 4 shows the 30% band midpoint and the 40% top, and the 50%/30% scenario range around this base.

challenges.challenge: The base waste mark is the Q3 2026 trough, and the report never explains it. Waste plus EV was 91.8% x US$25.733m = US$23.623m in 1H (US$11.8m a quarter) but 71% x US$44.4m = US$31.524m in 9M, so Q3 is US$7.901m waste-plus-EV (waste-only US$6.3m, F222) - a 47% fall in quarterly waste-only EBITDA while 9M waste revenue rose 41% (S27). S25 discloses a one-off refinancing expense at the waste entities without an amount, and F222 is a residual of two rounded share disclosures; the 9M LK segment note is still unfiled. The choice is dispositive: the Q3 mark gives US$106.2m equity and Rp312 (REDUCE); the 9M average gives US$218.7m and Rp430.3 (F204/F206, ADD).
challenges.answer: Filed the 9M consolidated LK (S28) and used it. The waste segment note (p.149) shows revenue US$157.320m, cost of revenue US$136.322m, a 13.3% gross margin and a US$4.288m operating loss. The Q3 fall is largely non-recurring: a US$1.789m AEI goodwill impairment and US$1.747m realised swap loss sit above EBITDA, and the finance-cost other line is US$15.425m against US$3.525m. The base is now the 9M-average annualisation of US$42.032m, marking waste equity at US$218.732m; the Q3 trough of US$31.604m is the explicit bear. Adding the two above-EBITDA items back gives US$33.435m for the 9M, or US$44.580m annualised, disclosed as the upper end.

challenges.challenge: The base stacks four conservative choices and discloses them but never weights them: Q3 trough waste mark, 40% top-of-band discount, half-haircut receivable and 25% minority. At the 30% card midpoint the target is Rp346.5 (F205) and at the 9M-average waste mark it is Rp430.3 (F206), while the 50/25/25 engine weights run from the 40% base only, so the weighted target 312 is not the midpoint of the disclosed range (the report's own driver-weighted figure is Rp334.7, F159). The consolidated FY2026E EBITDA margin is also 16.0% (Q4E US$10.25m) versus the 9M actual 17.3% (Q3 US$18.7m) even though Q4 revenue uses the Q3 run-rate; that 1.3pp squeeze comes from the inferred 17.6% D&A ratio and keeps the calibration gap at 4.2pp under the 5pp gate.
challenges.answer: The base now sits at the 9M-average mark and the D&A ratio is the 9M implied 18.9% rather than the 17.6% first-half inference, so FY2026E EBITDA margin is no longer below the 9M actual. The three disclosed alternatives are probability-weighted 25/50/25 (F159 = Rp437.4): trough Rp227.3, 9M base Rp419.1, bull Rp684.0. The 30% card midpoint on the 9M base is Rp471.4 (F205), a BUY; the Q3-trough midpoint after the closure provision is Rp333.5 (F248), a HOLD at the current price.

challenges.challenge: The base assigns zero value to the HPS commitment of up to S$555m (US$408m at SGD/USD 1.36) and assumes "no large acquisition", although S26 says the proceeds are for organic and inorganic Asian waste expansion and S27 says the transaction is pending only on realisation. The report's own peer-multiple case is Rp429 (F164) and the deployment case is described in §5, but the engine bull only narrows the discount to 30%, giving Rp346 - a -5.8% return, i.e. a "bull" that is a HOLD. The operating upside therefore never reaches the probability-weighted target.
challenges.answer: Added a dated, valued HPS-deployment bull to the 25% bull weight: the peer-multiple case gives Rp574.1 at the warranted discount (F164) and Rp684.0 with the discount at the card midpoint and coal at its plan upper bound (F158). The base still values the HPS money at zero at inception, but now justifies it: the waste mark is the ordinary/common equity after the preference claim, the terms and coupon are undisclosed, and paying for cash before it is invested and before the coupon is known would double-count the deployment. The 25/50/25 weighted target is Rp437.4, an ADD.

challenges.challenge: The 25% bear shocks only the holdco discount (50% to Rp278, -24.5%), so the report's own operating downside carries no probability weight: Q3 waste run-rate persisting or falling, the US$85.5m goodwill (P/BV Rp108 on full impairment, F210), the 55-83% preference coupon and 0.46x 9M CFO/EBITDA (F156) all sit outside the bear. The Rp200 "SELL corner" (F157) is a driver fact, not the bear scenario, and the probability-weighted target remains 312.
challenges.answer: The 25% bear is now an operating bear, not a discount shock: the Q3 trough annualisation (US$31.604m) at the 7.0x low-end multiple with a ten-point wider discount gives Rp227.3 (F157), a SELL.
